edits.before: Patch-seq mapping of layer 4 interneurons onto transcriptomic SST types supports the view that layer-4-targeting SOM-positive cells form a single morphological population, the non-Martinotti cells, whose axons remain in layer 4 rather than ascending to layer 1 {cite:p}`Scala2019`. Paired recordings across two sensory areas instead found strong morphological differences among layer 4 SST cells, which fell into the non-Martinotti subclass in somatosensory cortex but showed Martinotti-like features in visual cortex {cite:p}`Rachel2025`. The disagreement is about whether non-Martinotti identity belongs to the layer or to the area; it is open,
edits.after: Patch-seq mapping of layer 4 interneurons onto transcriptomic SST types sets the earlier view — that layer-4-targeting SOM-positive cells form a single morphological population, the non-Martinotti cells, whose axons remain in layer 4 rather than ascending to layer 1 — against its own result: non-fast-spiking SOM-positive neurons in visual cortex layer 4 are predominantly Martinotti cells, in contrast to somatosensory cortex layer 4 where almost all SOM-positive neurons are non-Martinotti, and the two correspond to different transcriptomic types {cite:p}`Scala2019`. Paired recordings across two sensory areas report the same areal split, finding strong morphological differences among layer 4 SST cells, which fell into the non-Martinotti subclass in somatosensory cortex but showed Martinotti-like features in visual cortex {cite:p}`Rachel2025`. The disagreement is between the earlier single-population view, in which non-Martinotti identity belongs to layer 4, and these two studies, in which it belongs to the area; it is open,
edits.reason: MISATTRIBUTED: attribution reversed to the paper's own result; neighbouring clauses adjusted for coherence

edits.before: Dense electron-microscopic reconstruction of mouse visual cortex reaches a compatible conclusion for cells identified as putative SST interneurons by arbour morphology rather than marker expression: inhibitory connectivity there is organised by fine morphological type rather than by cardinal marker class {cite:p}`SchneiderMizell2025`.
edits.after: Dense electron-microscopic reconstruction of mouse visual cortex reaches a compatible conclusion without molecular labels: inhibitory neurons show widespread target specificity, and groups with similar subclass-level targeting differ in which postsynaptic compartment they target, an organising principle for inhibitory connectivity that the authors describe as complementary to, but distinct from, cell types {cite:p}`SchneiderMizell2025`.
